Scalise: Foundry School Will Help America Out-Build and Out-Compete China | Congressman Steve Scalise Skip to main content Scalise: Foundry School Will Help America Out-Build and Out-Compete China September 3, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C.— This morning, House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.) joined Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Under Secretary of State Jacob Helberg for the launch of Foundry School at the Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace. The Leader highlighted America’s manufacturing comeback under President Trump and the importance of preparing the next generation of industry leaders and staying ahead of China. Image Click here or the image above to view Leader Scalise's full remarks. Remarks Below As Delivered: “I want to start by first congratulating Vice President Vance, Secretary Rubio, Undersecretary Helberg, Stanford University, and all the university and business leaders who have worked so hard to make Foundry School possible.  "What you're launching today comes at an incredibly exciting time for our country. "When President Trump was swept back into office, he made it clear that American manufacturing was going to be at the heart of America's golden age.  "For too long, we watched factories shutter and good-paying jobs leave our shores.  "President Trump promised we were going to reverse that trend and bring manufacturing back to America.  "And that's exactly what's happening. U.S. manufacturing activity surged in July at the strongest rate in over four years. “More than 18,000 manufacturing jobs have been created this year alone. And manufacturing wages are up more than 4% over the last year, putting more money in the pockets of American workers.  "That is a remarkable turnaround. And Republicans in Congress have been proud to work with President Trump to help make this possible.  "Last year, we passed the transformational Working Families Tax Cut to make America the best place in the world to build, invest, and create good-paying jobs. “Now we have to keep building on that momentum, because at the same time American manufacturing is coming back, there is a global race underway
